### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **2** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d4aaeaf0e2eb39ac574f1ba171a88535f9a678b4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e4103b9520b786e6c109c0fec994406479ec1be8` — the merge of head `9d9bdd96b2457b51ff32a86c3928c73c5771ad98` into base `d4aaeaf0e2eb39ac574f1ba171a88535f9a678b4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e4103b9520b786e6c109c0fec994406479ec1be8 && git checkout e4103b9520b786e6c109c0fec994406479ec1be8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d4aaeaf0e2eb39ac574f1ba171a88535f9a678b4 9d9bdd96b2457b51ff32a86c3928c73c5771ad98 && git checkout -B drift-repro d4aaeaf0e2eb39ac574f1ba171a88535f9a678b4 && git merge --no-ff 9d9bdd96b2457b51ff32a86c3928c73c5771ad98

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d4aaeaf0e2eb39ac574f1ba171a88535f9a678b4
```

## Contract review

Read-only inputs: PR #22962's body, file list (94) and commits since `813dfed93e` (the merge `a805619472` of `main` `f931e765b7`, then six fast-forward commits); the net three-dot diff against `main` (94 files, +1243 / −4180, merge base `f931e765b7`); card #23056 (body and 11 comments, the claim 6136942521, the S8 dispatch 6137095247, the main-red ask 6137492570 and PR #23159, the dev report 6140041869); #15204's 6118994290, 6110777865 and 6116546399; AGENTS.md's deletion clause (ruling record 6120820653); the 48 check-runs on the head. `main` has since moved to `d4aaeaf0e2` (232 files); of the 94, only `mail-message-pool-read-gate` moved on `main`, and to the same blob.

### ① Derived judgments

**Test-only, confirmed.** 74 modified, 16 removed, 4 added. Every path is a `*.test.ts`, a test helper or config of the private dogfood package (`test/catalog-permission-set.ts`, `vitest.config.ts`), or a testkit under `src/__tests__/`. No product source.

**The 16 deletions against E1 → A, E3 → A, E4 → A and the deletion clause.** Reading applied: the epic seat ruled "Tests go in T-PRs ahead of" stage 8 (6110777865), so a pin whose code S8 removes is deleted here; the clause is then met in substance, not in letter, and the window between S8-T and S8 is the ruled cost. Per file:

- `core/src/security/row-active.test.ts`: `isRowActive` has no runtime caller on `main` (only the core export and comments name it); S8 removes the export (its changeset lists it). Substance.
- `bootstrap-platform-admin-refused-existence-read.test.ts` (D's version, #22169): the legacy `sys_permission_set` row read's refused leg, which E6 removes. The survivor, an unnamed legacy admin grant mints no second administrator, is pinned in `grant-readers-unnamed-grant` (plugin-security and plugin-auth copies), unit layer. Substance.
- `objects/clone-carryover.test.ts` and pin 6 of `packaged-permission-set-lock.test.ts` (#11703, #11992): the `clone_permission_set` action on the retired object. The surviving clone door is pinned on `main` by `runtime/src/domains/permission-set-clone.test.ts` (the copied set `objects`, `fields`, `systemPermissions`, `tabPermissions`, `rowLevelSecurity`, `description`; `adminScope` in the dropped list; the walled refusal), unit layer. Clause met.
- `sys-position`, `sys-permission-set`, `sys-capability` `.organization-unique.test.ts`, `sys-capability-deactivation-claim.test.ts`, and the retired-object cases of `rbac-objects`, `reserved-identity-names`, `managed-by-system-data`, `sys-security-assignment-display-title`, `rbac-objects-bulk-exposure`: declaration-shape and string pins of the four objects; the driver-side unique-scope suites they mirrored are untouched. Substance.
- `position-write-through.test.ts` (901 lines): the write-through, Q1 and Q2, the one-holder 409 and the ADR-0048 N.2/N.3 data-door refusals; S8 unwires the middleware. Q3's registry seam (422 NAMESPACE_CONFLICT) survives and is pinned in `objectql/src/registry-security-catalog-namespace.test.ts`, `runtime/src/standalone-stack-security-catalog-one-holder.test.ts` and the dogfood `security-catalog-cold-boot-environment-holder`. Substance.
- Dogfood `declared-position-provenance`, `permission-set-write-through-package-binding`, `position-environment-write-through`, `position-held-name-setup-create`, `two-doors-permission` (its "env door" delete is `DELETE /data/sys_permission_set/:id`), `showcase-permission-projection`: data-door and projector behaviour. Their surviving halves, 403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE at `/meta` for a packaged set and Q3, are pinned at unit layers in metadata-protocol (`protocol.packaged-base-refusal`, `sys-metadata-repository.package-writability`), plugin-security (`packaged-permission-set-lock*`) and objectql. Clause met for those halves.
- `permission-set-lock-row-provenance` (#21789): half data door, half metadata door plus the layered read. The metadata-door half survives S8 and is pinned in the kept `packaged-permission-set-lock.test.ts` (the hydrated row with `_provenance: 'org'`, #21789 named), unit layer. Clause met.
- `walled-catalog-data-door.test.ts` (#22895, added to `main` after S8-T's base): the clause finding below. Not met in letter.

No deleted file pins a behaviour that survives S8 without a pin at a layer at least as close to the code. Not a FAIL.

**The clause finding, `walled-catalog-data-door.test.ts`.** On `main` the door is registered (`security-plugin.ts:4367-4369`, one middleware per object in `WALLED_CATALOG_OBJECT_TYPES`). The deleted file pins six things: the walled create refusal; the walled update and delete refusal with the row untouched; the operator rung and a system write admitted; a tenant rung below the operator refused; the judged set being exactly the three catalog objects. After this PR the only remaining pin is the data-door case of `wall-catalog-refusal.dogfood.test.ts`, create only, now `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` while the row objects are registered and `404 OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` after. The `/meta` wall case in the same file pins a different code path, the metadata door's wall (#22935, #23003). So one case of six remains, at the dogfood layer, which PR and queue CI do not run (#22998). Verdict on the clause: not met in letter; met in substance only under the ruled T-PR design and because S8 unregisters the door with the write-throughs; the five other cases have no pin anywhere in the window. The PR body and the comments in `builtin-positions.boot.test.ts` (at the dropped key and in `refusalGoldenFor`) say the walled create refusal "stays pinned at the `/meta` wall": that names the wrong door. Fix: (a) restore the file in S8-T, which is `main`'s bytes and green on `main`, and delete it in S8 together with the door (the S8 build-ahead already resolves the door's unregistration, `c211fdd416`); or (b) the seat records on the PR that the clause is waived for a pin whose code the next PR removes, and corrects the attribution. The attribution correction blocks; the restore is recommended under the ruled design and becomes mandatory if S8 does not land right after S8-T.

**Weakened or removed assertions in kept files.**

- `builtin-positions.boot.test.ts`: `withLegacyCatalogTables` registers the four tables beside `securityObjects`; the walled scenarios drop the golden key `control: create a position row` (was `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`) on both trees, while the insert still runs. Every other key is unchanged: the two built-in row refusals, the dangling and row-only assignment refusals, the stack-declared assignment control. The dropped key could have been kept where the plugin declares `sys_position`, the registration-guarded pattern this PR uses for its censuses, which keeps the unit pin on `main` at no cost on the S8 tree. Not a mask; a dropped pin on `main` for the window.
- `wall-catalog-refusal.dogfood.test.ts`: the data-door case spans by `ql.getObject?.(object)`; a missing `getObject` would make the test expect 404 on `main` and fail loudly, not pass vacuously. Verified on `main`: the suite exists and pins the walled `/meta` create, save and delete refusals (403 FORBIDDEN), the data-door create refusal (403 PERMISSION_DENIED), the clone-door refusal, and the assign and operator controls; the `/meta`, clone and control cases are unchanged here.
- plugin-auth `grant-readers-unnamed-grant` and `grant-readers-by-name.golden`: `withLegacyPermissionSetTable` adds the `sys_permission_set` shape only when the manifest does not declare it; `seedLegacyPlatformBucket` then writes the platform-bucket rows, and the suite reads a seeded row's id to write a legacy `permission_set_id` (the case "writing the legacy id moves no standing"). The seed is meaningful: it models the existing database whose grants carry legacy ids (ADR-0131 D10). The shape is reached through a copy inside plugin-auth (`src/__tests__/legacy-catalog-objects.testkit.ts`, one object), not a relative import out of the package, so `check:cross-package-test-inputs` has nothing to flag; it sits in the green Lint & Repo Gates. Within the rules.
- `cleanup-package-permissions.test.ts`: the sweep is handed D's `UninstallDeclared` shape `{ permission: [...] }`; the fixture drops the `sys_position_permission_set` rows and gives every grant a name; the exact totals (`sets`, `positionBindings`, the legacy-id `userGrants`) become `toMatchObject` on the name-leg fields and `refused` becomes `toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(4)` (was 7). D's two named-grant pins are restated: "revokes every grant naming a declared set, and only those" is exact (4 grants, exact survivors); the control "handed no names" keeps the pin that a grant naming an un-handed set survives (`arrayContaining` over the un-handed grants). Spans correctly; the counts should be re-tightened after S8.
- `catalog-reference-report.test.ts`: `resolves` for `twin_lead` (the position backfill's doing) is no longer asserted; the backfill-ledger case is deleted; the `kernel:bootstrapped` handler floor goes 3 to 2. `grant-permission-set-name-backfill.test.ts`: handlers `toHaveLength(3)` becomes `toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(2)`. Spans; re-tighten after S8.
- `tenant-wall-post-hook-image.test.ts`: the `[#20013]` ADR-0094 data-door case is removed (the door S8 unwires); the tenant-wall post-hook cases stay.
- The clone-route prose pins (`protocol.packaged-base-refusal`, `sys-metadata-repository.package-writability`, `rest-meta-packaged-action-permission-refusal`): the sentence is pinned up to `POST /api/v1/` and from ` with a new name).`, with `sentenceMatches` requiring one `/api/v1/` path between. Spans; pin the clone door's route after S8.
- Floors: `platform-page-i18n-parity` label maps 44 to 38 (measured on `main` + S8) and record pages 3 to 2; `organization-ownership-inventory` registry 80 to 75; `canonical-expression-envelopes` 3 to 2. Floors, not masks.
- `tenancy-by-object-classification.test.ts`: the `sys_permission_set` `global` assertions become a loop over `PLATFORM_OBJECT_TENANCY`; after S8 the inventory holds no `global` entry, so the discriminating half of #8672 then pins nothing. Accept, or re-pin with a fixture entry after S8.
- `validate-capability-references.test.ts`: the `sys_capability` seed-row source case is removed (S8 removes that source); the one-line verdict is pinned by prefix and suffix. `me-apps-and-everyone-baseline`: the read "no everyone row is written" is dropped rather than registration-guarded; the unit pin stays in `builtin-positions.boot` (lines 512 and 523). `showcase-permission-zoo`: the three junction-write gate cases (ADR-0090 D5/D9/D12 on `sys_position_permission_set` rows) go with the object; see ③ item 5. `get-effective-object-permissions`: the parity case moves from `sys_position`/`sys_permission_set` to `sys_user_position`/`sys_user_permission_set`, which `organization_admin` still names read-only (the kept `rbac-objects` loop). `dangling-reference-audit`: the fixture is renamed to a surviving table; the shape is the fixture's own.
- Censuses guarded by `getObject` (`showcase-permission-seeding`, `builtin-capabilities.boot`, `permission-set-clone-door`, `showcase-d7-default-profile`, `standalone-stack-seeder-declaration-copy`): the "no row" pins hold on `main` and are vacuous after S8, by design.

**The testkits.** `plugin-security/src/__tests__/legacy-catalog-objects.testkit.ts` (521 lines): four `ObjectSchema.create` declarations with fields, indexes, the `enable` flags and, for `sys_position`, the `reserved_identity_name` validation copied from `main`'s object; `LEGACY_CATALOG_OBJECTS` and `withLegacyCatalogTables()`; no hooks, actions, list views or functions beyond the registration filter. Field lists match `main`'s objects for `sys_position`, `sys_capability` and `sys_position_permission_set`; `sys_permission_set` carries two columns `main`'s object no longer declares, `drift_status` and `drift_detail` (present at S8-T's base `eab7236ff7`, removed by D `c8a9783eca`). No suite reads them; harmless, but the header's "as the last release that declared the object stored them" should say which release. The plugin-auth copy: one object, fields and indexes, `withLegacyPermissionSetTable()` over the manifest's untyped list. Neither masks behaviour: the plugin's own middleware is what the suites exercise; the tables are only the rows' home.

**The mail-pool hunk.** `packages/qa/dogfood/test/mail-message-pool-read-gate.dogfood.test.ts` is blob `adb8b0fa73` on the head and on current `origin/main` (`b8f226c440`, PR #23159); the two-dot diff is empty. A no-op at the next `main` merge.

**Both trees.** Tree A (`main` + S8-T) is CI-verified on this head: Test Core 1/6 to 6/6, the Type Check lanes and every Lint lane are `success`. Tree B (`main` + S8-T + S8) exists only as the dev's never-pushed scratch tree. The dev's account names each file the S8 build-ahead reported red, with counts at shas: `builtin-positions.boot` 4 failed at `008ca32a75`, 52/52 at `d426f922ed`; the plugin-auth pair 9 failed at `008ca32a75` ("Object 'sys_permission_set' not found"), 9/9 at `e40fe491c1`; cli 1 failed (38 maps under a floor of 39), 35/35 at the floor of 38; plus plugin-security 185 files / 3815 passed, dogfood 24/24 (280 tests), typecheck 67 tasks. Declared narrowing: those changed unit files and the plugin-auth typecheck ran outside the verify lock at `--maxWorkers=1`. The claim is supported by the evidence, file by file, and not verified here; nothing in the diff contradicts it. The dogfood shards did not run on this head (skipped under #22998), so the 22 dogfood files have no CI record before `main`'s next full battery.

### ② Semver level

No changeset, `skip-changeset`, `Clause-②: no`. Nothing published moves: every file is a test, a test helper or config of the private `@objectstack/dogfood`, or a testkit under `src/__tests__/` of `@objectstack/plugin-security` or `@objectstack/plugin-auth`. Both packages build with tsup from their entry points (`exports` `.`, and `./rate-limit-storage` for plugin-auth); no non-test source imports a testkit, so none reaches `dist`, and `files` ships `dist` only. `packages/spec/src/system/constants/system-names.test.ts` loses its `POSITION` and `PERMISSION_SET` assertions while the constants stay (S8 removes them). Confirmed.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Act before the queue: the PR body's pin attribution.** The body says the walled create refusal "stays pinned at the `/meta` wall by `wall-catalog-refusal.dogfood.test.ts`" (and `builtin-positions.boot.test.ts` repeats it in two comments). That names the wrong door: the data-door refusal (`walled-catalog-data-door.ts`, #22895) is pinned only by that file's data-door case, registration-conditional, dogfood layer. Correct the body sentence; the test comments can follow in S8 or with the restore in item 2.
2. **The deletion clause, `walled-catalog-data-door.test.ts`.** Not met in letter (①). Recommended: restore the file in S8-T and delete it in S8 with the door. If the seat instead rules the clause satisfied in substance for a pin whose code the next PR removes, that ruling belongs on the PR, not only in the dev report's deviations. Either way, if S8 does not land right after S8-T the restore stops being optional: five of the door's six cases are unpinned in the window and PR and queue CI run no dogfood.
3. **`builtin-positions.boot`'s walled create key**: dropped on `main` where a registration-guarded span was available. Recommended with the restore; not blocking.
4. **Spans to re-tighten after S8**, needing a carrier (the S8 dispatch forbids S8 from editing S8-T's files, so 8-post): `cleanup-package-permissions` (`toMatchObject`, `toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(4)`), `grant-permission-set-name-backfill` (handlers at least 2), `catalog-reference-report` (handlers at least 2, `objectContaining`), the clone-route prose pins (`/api/v1/` prefix), `wall-catalog-refusal` (403 or 404 by registration), `tenancy-by-object-classification` (no `global` entry), `protocol.uninstall-cleanups-runner` (`objectContaining(request)`). None masks a regression on `main`; each is looser than before.
5. **Junction gates retired without a metadata-door counterpart pinned.** ADR-0090 D5/D9 (a high-privilege set bound to the `everyone` anchor is refused) and D12 (`manageBindings: false`) were pinned on `sys_position_permission_set` writes in `showcase-permission-zoo`; after S8 a position's sets are its definition's `permissionSets`. Whether the metadata door enforces the same is NOT MEASURED here; the stage-8 report lists the delegated-admin gate and the SP catalog gates as 8-post residue. Name it on 8-post.
6. **Dev deviations, answered.** The scratch tree by cherry-pick: acceptable, the S8 branch carries a superseded D. The walled door aligned with `c211fdd416` before the ruling: consistent with the ruling that followed. Unlocked runs for the changed unit files: a declared narrowing; tree A is CI-covered. Two commits superseded by rulings (`c0dc292ae8` by `d426f922ed`; `08524a1563` widened by `e40fe491c1`): history kept. The walled-door clause deviation: item 2. #23159's body cites the earlier product tree; the report carries the `121847a7d5` run. `main` moved after the merge (now `d4aaeaf0e2`): the overlap is the identical mail-pool blob; no test file added on `main` since `f931e765b7` reads the four objects; modified ones were not swept here. Model-free `Co-Authored-By` trailers on all seven commits since the handoff, as the card requires. Open questions: none. Out-of-scope findings: #23159 is landed; the S8 scratch-resolution note is S8's; `check:type-check-debt`'s unlocked build is an acceptance note.
7. **Check-runs on `e40fe491c1`**: 48, 38 `success`, 10 `skipped`, none running. Skipped: Check Changeset (`skip-changeset`), the three Dogfood Regression Gate shards, Dogfood Verify CLI, Temporal Conformance, Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke, and the label-triggered re-runs of Auto Label and Check PR Size (their first runs `success`). The gate verdicts are green; the dogfood half of this PR has no CI verdict until `main`'s full battery, which the seat reads after the merge as it did for #23159.
8. **Form.** Still a draft; Tier H by size (5,423 changed lines, 77% deletion), so the maintainer's approval or merge is required; the 维护者速读 is marked 草稿 with 席位意见 empty, for the seat to fill before readying. NOT MEASURED: tree B (no CI run exists); the dogfood files on this head (no CI run exists); the testkit's `drift_status` and `drift_detail` columns' effect on any upgrade-path suite (none reads them).

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `9d9bdd96b2457b51ff32a86c3928c73c5771ad98`
Local-runs: none

Delta record after the PASS 6140381269 on `e40fe491c1`. Read-only inputs: PR #22962's body (as edited by the seat for patch round 1, `updated_at` 2026-10-13T08:10Z), its file list (93) and its nine commits; the delta `e40fe491c1..9d9bdd96b2` (one fast-forward commit, parent `e40fe491c1`, committed 2026-10-13T07:18Z); the net diff against `main` (merge base `f931e765b7`; `origin/main` read at `d889448b93`); card #23056's body and all 13 comments (the claim 6136942521, the S8 dispatch 6137095247, the dev reports 6140041869 and 6141188275, the seat's correction 6140398039); the prior record 6140381269 and the docs-drift comment on the PR; the 48 check-runs on this head; `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/walled-catalog-data-door.test.ts`, `walled-catalog-data-door.ts`, `security-plugin.ts` and `manifest.ts` on `origin/main`. Nothing built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

**The delta is exactly the two files the patch round named.** `git diff --name-status e40fe491c1..9d9bdd96b2`: `A packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/walled-catalog-data-door.test.ts`, `M packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/builtin-positions.boot.test.ts`; nothing else. The restored file is blob `003a885f3f` on the head, on `origin/main` and at the merge base `f931e765b7`, so it leaves the PR diff (the three-dot diff against `origin/main` and the two-dot diff against `f931e765b7` both read 93 files, 74 modified, 15 removed, 4 added, +1,255 / −3,950; the prior record's 94 was this file as the 16th removal). No `main` merge, no rebase, no force-push: `e40fe491c1` is the head's parent and the branch's eight earlier commits are unchanged. No other change exists to review.

**`builtin-positions.boot` is a faithful both-trees pin, and no weakening on `main`.** The guard is `PLUGIN_DECLARES_POSITION_ROWS`, a module-level `securityObjects.some(...)` over the object name `sys_position`, read off `./manifest.js`'s `securityObjects`, the plugin's own declared object list (on `main` it lists `SysPosition` first; `withLegacyCatalogTables` adds only the tables that list does not declare, so it does not feed the guard). `judgesCreate(scenario)` is `posture === 'single' || PLUGIN_DECLARES_POSITION_ROWS`; `refusalGoldenFor` for a walled scenario is `{ ...REFUSAL_GOLDEN, 'control: create a position row': { ok: false, code: 'PERMISSION_DENIED', status: 403 } }` while the object is declared, which is byte-equal to `main`'s golden at `f931e765b7`, and the create-less golden only once it is not. On `main` the observed key set and the golden are therefore identical to `main`'s own: the walled create is judged and expected `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` in all four walled scenarios, the `single` scenarios keep `ok: true`, and every other key (the dangling and row-only assignment refusals, the stack-declared control, the two built-in row refusals) is untouched. On the S8 tree the key leaves; the insert still runs and is not asserted, which is the designed vacuity.
